title: urnetwork / provider quality probes
description: Continuous provider quality probes (qualityprobe fleetprobe, run by the taskworker): fleet state, probe outcomes, breakdowns by provider country and by probe target, failure classes, latency, exit placement, blackhole, bandwidth, and pass health. Fleet snapshot panels select one most-recent Taskworker refresh and go no-data after 15 minutes; monitor signal §2.23 is the authoritative direct-database alert.

panels.title: how the probes work, and what a systematic issue looks like

options.content:
**What the probes are.** The taskworker runs the provider egress probes (qualityprobe `fleetprobe`) as recurring `pending_task` shards. Each **full probe** opens a tunnel pinned to one provider, warms it up on the operator's own `/my-ip-info` echo, which answers with the exit address the platform saw (the server places it with GeoLite2: the city only within the confident radius, else the region or country; no vendor is asked, so there are no hosting, proxy or mobile verdicts), loads a sample of real sites through the same tunnel (per class: `dns`, `connectivity`, `cdn`, `site`, only sites compatible with the provider's place; each load gets up to three browser-shaped tries spaced minutes apart, and a load a lost tunnel never reached is *not measured*, not failed), optionally samples **active bandwidth**, and reports the attempt outcome. A separate **blackhole** schedule checks whether a provider carries anything at all; a failed check is not a verdict, and a provider is dark only after three failed checks in a row. Findings are written to Postgres through the operator ingest API; the metrics on this board are recorded by the taskworker at the moment each finding is submitted (`urnetwork_egress_probe_*`), and the fleet gauges are re-counted from the durable tables at most once a minute.

**Reading systematic issues.** A prober fault looks the same for every provider: one failure class dominates the attempts (the *failed attempts / min by class* panel and the *dominant failure class* stat), every country's fail rate jumps at once, and the pass rows show due queues pinned at the batch limit or batch errors. The prober also judges itself: the *fleet dark share* or *fleet failure share by class* over its 20 % line, *batch guard trips*, and the prober-side attempt classes (`health_not_run`, `run_not_measured`, `no_exit_ip`, `run_batch_guard`) are its own misses, never verdicts on providers. A bad **target** looks like one destination failing for every country (row *by target*) while its class siblings stay green. A bad **region** looks like every class failing for one country (row *by country*) while the same targets stay green elsewhere. A **fleet** problem (providers really degrading) shows as rising `dead`/`degraded` health results with the pass rows healthy.

**Data not collected today.** Per-check latency is recorded only for successful checks (a failed check's elapsed time is not exported). The provider's app version, transport and IP family are not part of the probe record, so there is no breakdown by those. Bandwidth samples carry the sample source only, not the country.

panels.title: fleet state (re-counted from the durable tables at most once a minute)
healthy providers
panels.description: Providers whose last egress health result passed every scored check. Systematic: this number collapsing within one pass while the pass rows show no errors means the prober's tunnels broke, not the fleet.

targets.expr: sum(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_health_providers{env="$env",state="healthy"} and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} > time() - 900) and (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} <= time() + 30)))

panels.title: degraded providers
panels.description: Providers whose last health result passed some but not all scored checks.

targets.expr: sum(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_health_providers{env="$env",state="degraded"} and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} > time() - 900) and (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} <= time() + 30)))

panels.title: dead providers
panels.description: Providers whose last health result passed no scored check. Systematic: a jump here paired with a jump in one failure class is the prober, not the providers.

targets.expr: sum(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_health_providers{env="$env",state="dead"} and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} > time() - 900) and (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} <= time() + 30)))

panels.title: current proved failures
panels.description: Currently eligible providers with a proved current failure in the bounded failure vocabulary, the failure count of monitor signal §2.23: tunnel_failed, contract_failed, submit_failed, health_not_run, run_not_measured, no_exit_ip, run_batch_guard and unknown_failure, plus the consensus classes no_consensus, locate_failed and not_confident, which the prober no longer reports and which read zero once their attempts age out of the six-hour retry window. health_not_run, run_not_measured, no_exit_ip and run_batch_guard are the probe's own misses (a run that never started, measured nothing, got no answer from the operator's /ip echo, or was held back by the run batch guard), not verdicts on the provider's traffic; they count because a fleet failing that way is the prober. Unobserved and inconsistent states stay in the population but are not mislabeled as provider failures; *eligible fleet by probe outcome* splits the count by class.

targets.expr: sum(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_attempt_providers{env="$env",result=~"tunnel_failed|contract_failed|health_not_run|run_not_measured|no_exit_ip|submit_failed|run_batch_guard|no_consensus|locate_failed|not_confident|unknown_failure"} and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} > time() - 900) and (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} <= time() + 30)))

panels.title: current success
panels.description: Currently eligible providers with a trusted submitted location and no retained nonempty failure that makes the state failed or ambiguous.

targets.expr: sum(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_attempt_providers{env="$env",result="ok"} and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} > time() - 900) and (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} <= time() + 30)))

panels.title: dominant failure class
panels.description: The population-aware fleet diagnosis: set when one known current failure class covers at least 90% of the complete eligible population, with at least 20 observed outcomes. Unknown, inconsistent, and unobserved states cannot manufacture dominance. Empty is good.

targets.expr: max by (class) ((urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_dominant_failure{env="$env"} == 1) and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} > time() - 900) and (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} <= time() + 30)))

panels.title: dominant class share
panels.description: Share of the complete current eligible population covered by the dominant known failure class; 0 when nothing dominates.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_dominant_share{env="$env"} and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} > time() - 900) and (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} <= time() + 30)))

panels.title: blackholed providers
panels.description: Providers currently dark: three failed blackhole checks in a row spanning at least 30 minutes by default, or a tls authentication failure, within the three-hour check max age (geomap §11.3). A single failed check is not dark.

targets.expr: sum(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_flagged_providers{env="$env",flag="blackholed"} and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} > time() - 900) and (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} <= time() + 30)))

panels.title: tls authentication failed
panels.description: Providers whose egress presented a certificate that could not authenticate the requested host: an interception signal, kept apart from the score.

targets.expr: sum(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_flagged_providers{env="$env",flag="tls_authentication_failed"} and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} > time() - 900) and (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} <= time() + 30)))

panels.title: eligible fleet by probe outcome
panels.description: Every currently eligible provider by reconstructed state: ok, a bounded current failure class, inconsistent, or unobserved. A known failure class covering at least 90% of the complete population is the common-prober signature; unknown values cannot establish it.

targets.expr: sum by (result) (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_attempt_providers{env="$env"} and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} > time() - 900) and (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} <= time() + 30)))

panels.title: fleet dark share
panels.description: The share of the providers with a current measured blackhole check that are dark by the consecutive-failure rule (geomap §11.3). A fleet over the dark batch guard's 20 % line is the prober until proven otherwise -- a request-shape, route or capacity fault, not a fifth of the providers going dark at once. The same gauge as the providers dashboard's, read from the one fresh taskworker snapshot like the rest of this row.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_dark_share{env="$env"} and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} > time() - 900) and (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} <= time() + 30)))

panels.title: fleet failure share by class
panels.description: The failed share of the scored loads, after retries, of the health runs measured within the prober-fault window (an hour by default), per class and over all of them (all). Over the 20 % prober-fault line in every class is a fault on the prober -- its request shape or its capacity -- not on the sites (monitor signal §2.19b), and the site pool refresh skips its run while the share of the loads that reached their provider is over the line, or while fewer than a fifth of the recent loads reached their provider at all (this panel counts every failure, a provider that was never reached included). Read from the one fresh taskworker snapshot like the rest of this row.

targets.expr: max by (class) (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_failure_share{env="$env"} and on(env,service,block,host,instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} > time() - 900) and (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker"} <= time() + 30)))

panels.title: probes succeeded (range)
panels.description: Full probe attempts that completed end to end in the selected range (filtered by country).

panels.title: probes failed (range)
panels.description: Full probe attempts that failed in the selected range (any class).

panels.title: success rate (range)
panels.description: Share of attempts that succeeded over the selected range. Systematic: a step change here with a flat provider count is the prober or the platform, not the providers.

panels.title: health checks ok (range)
panels.description: Individual egress health checks that passed in the range (filtered by class and destination).

panels.title: health checks failed (range)
panels.description: Individual egress health checks that failed in the range.

panels.title: blackhole checks failed (range)
panels.description: Blackhole checks in the range that measured the provider and failed after their retries (all_destinations_failed, tunnel_failed, tls_authentication_failed). A failed check is not a verdict: a provider is dark only after three in a row spanning at least 30 minutes, or at once on a tls authentication failure (geomap §11.3). Checks that measured nothing (not_measured) are the prober's lost path and are left out.

panels.title: probe attempts / min by result
panels.description: Rate of full probe attempts per minute split by outcome (ok or the failure class). Systematic: every class except one going to zero, or the total dropping to zero, points at the pass (see the last row), not at providers.

panels.title: probe success rate
panels.description: Share of attempts succeeding, over time. A cliff is the earliest single signal of a prober-side fault.

panels.title: failed attempts / min by class
panels.description: Failures by class: tunnel_failed (the pinned tunnel never came up: platform or prober connectivity), health_not_run (the health run never started: no budget left, a structural error, or the pass ended under it), run_not_measured (the tunnel died and could not be re-created, so nothing was measured), no_exit_ip (the operator's /ip echo never answered, so there was no exit to submit), run_batch_guard (the run's batch failed its scored loads together over the run guard line and was held back and re-queued), submit_failed (the operator API refused the finding, an exit GeoLite2 cannot place among them: server side), contract_failed. no_consensus, locate_failed and not_confident come only from probers that predate the /ip echo. One class carrying the whole area is a prober fault.

panels.title: health results / min by state
panels.description: Per-provider health outcomes as probed: healthy (every scored check ok), degraded, dead. The fleet gauges above are the durable last-known state; this is the live flow.

panels.title: attempts by country (range)
panels.description: Full probe attempts per provider egress country over the range, sorted by fail rate. Systematic (region): one country red on every class in the health table on the right while other countries stay green.

panels.title: health checks by country (range)
panels.description: Egress health loads per provider country over the range, after each load's retries (filter by class to isolate dns / connectivity / cdn / site). The fail rate is over the ok and failed loads: loads not measured and canaries are neither.

panels.title: attempt fail rate by country (top 10)
panels.description: Worst countries by attempt fail rate. Every country rising together is not a region problem.

panels.title: health check fail rate by class and country (top 10)
panels.description: Worst country+class pairs by health check fail rate: a single country with several classes listed is a region; a single class across many countries is a target class. The rate is over the ok and failed loads, as in the tables: loads not measured and canaries are neither.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (country, class) (rate(urnetwork_egress_probe_health_checks_by_country_total{env="$env",class=~"$class",country=~"$country",result="fail"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (country, class) (rate(urnetwork_egress_probe_health_checks_by_country_total{env="$env",class=~"$class",country=~"$country",result=~"ok|fail"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9))

panels.title: locations submitted / min by country (top 15)
panels.description: Egress locations the prober submitted per country. A country that stops appearing while its providers are still connected means those providers stopped being located.

panels.title: exit placements / min by precision
panels.description: How precisely GeoLite2 places the exit addresses the prober submits, by the resolution the ingest itself applies, so the label and the stored row agree (geomap §11.3): city when the record names one within the confident radius (25 km by default), region or country when it does not, and not placed when GeoLite2 has no country for the address, which the server refuses and the attempt reports as submit_failed. Filtered by the country GeoLite2 places the exit in. No vendor is asked where an exit is, so there are no hosting, proxy or mobile flags; a run whose /ip echo never answered submits no exit (see *exit address lookups / min*).

panels.title: health checks by destination (range)
panels.description: Every probe target over the range with its class, sorted by fail rate. Systematic (target): one destination red for every country while its class siblings are green; a whole class red means the class table itself (e.g. every CDN endpoint) or a prober-side header/verify change.

panels.title: health check fail rate by destination (top 15)
panels.description: Worst destinations by fail rate over time. The rate is over the ok and failed loads, as in the tables: loads not measured and canaries are neither.

panels.title: health check fail rate by class
panels.description: Fail rate per class, after each load's retries. There is no reputation class any more: its sites are ordinary site destinations, sampled and scored like the rest (geomap §11.3). The rate is over the ok and failed loads, as in the tables: loads not measured and canaries are neither.

panels.title: checks / min by destination (probe volume)
panels.description: How often each destination is exercised. A destination that goes flat at zero while the others continue has dropped out of the sampled table (removed, or its class sample shrank); the whole set going to zero is the pass, not the targets.

panels.title: checks / min by class
panels.description: Probe volume per class. Sample sizes never go below 3 per class, so a class disappearing means the class was not sampled at all.

panels.title: tls authentication failures by destination (range)
panels.description: Checks whose HTTPS peer could not authenticate the requested host. One destination alone: that site's certificate changed or is proxied; many destinations at once through the same providers: interception on the egress.

panels.title: tls authentication failures / min
panels.description: Rate of TLS authentication failures across all destinations.

panels.title: latency (successful health checks through the provider tunnel)
mean health check latency
panels.description: Fleet mean of successful check latency from cumulative sum/count samples. A shift for every class at once points to the tunnel path; one destination alone points to that target. Exact one-minute maxima are shown separately without classic histogram buckets.

panels.title: mean / latest one-minute max latency by class
panels.description: Aggregatable fleet mean and the exact maximum from each process's latest fresh one-minute interval. The maximum is joined to its observation timestamp so an idle destination cannot look current.

targets.expr: max by (class) (urnetwork_egress_probe_health_check_interval_max_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",instance!="",class=~"$class",destination=~"$destination"} and on (env, service, block, host, instance, destination, class) (urnetwork_egress_probe_health_check_interval_max_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",instance!="",class=~"$class",destination=~"$destination"} >= time() - 120 and urnetwork_egress_probe_health_check_interval_max_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",instance!="",class=~"$class",destination=~"$destination"} <= time() + 30))

panels.title: mean latency by destination (range, slowest 20)
panels.description: Slowest destinations by aggregatable mean over the selected range. Use the adjacent fresh maximum panel for exact tail events.

panels.title: exit address, prober-side outcomes, blackhole checks, bandwidth
exit address lookups / min
panels.description: The prober's only source for where an exit is: the operator's own /my-ip-info echo, fetched through the provider's tunnel as each run's warm-up (geomap §11.3). exit submitted is the runs whose echo answered, their exits sent to the server to be placed (filtered by the exit's country); no_exit_ip is the runs that measured loads but never got an answer, so there was no exit to submit (filtered by the provider's last known country). no_exit_ip in every country at once is the echo itself -- its reachability from the open internet, its certificate, or the api behind it -- not the providers (monitor signal §2.23); in one country only, the echo is unreachable or blocked from there.

panels.title: prober-side attempt outcomes by country (range)
panels.description: Full-run attempts over the range that ended on the prober's side, by provider country and class: health_not_run (the run never started), run_not_measured (its tunnel died and could not be re-created), no_exit_ip (the operator's /ip echo never answered) and run_batch_guard (its batch's scored loads failed together over the run guard line, so the batch was held back and re-queued). None is a verdict on the provider's traffic. One country at the top is that place's route or the echo blocked there; every country together is the prober.

panels.title: blackhole checks / min by result
panels.description: Blackhole check outcomes after each check's retries: ok, all_destinations_failed (no sampled connectivity destination answered any attempt), tunnel_failed (no tunnel to the provider), tls_authentication_failed, or not_measured (the tunnel died and could not be re-created, or the dark batch guard discarded the batch's negatives; nothing counts against the provider). A failed check is not a verdict: a provider is dark only after three in a row spanning at least 30 minutes (geomap §11.3). all_destinations_failed rising with tunnel_failed flat is providers failing checks; tunnel_failed or not_measured rising is the prober's connectivity.

panels.title: bandwidth samples p50 / p95 by source
panels.description: Active bandwidth through provider tunnels by sample source (operator or cdn), plus the sample rate. Both sources collapsing together is the prober's own uplink.

panels.title: pass health (the taskworker shards that run the probes)
providers due per batch (last)
panels.description: Providers the server handed to the last batch of each schedule. Pinned at the batch limit means the due queue is never drained (the prober is falling behind or every attempt fails and re-queues); flat at zero means nothing is due or the due query fails (see errors).

panels.title: batches / min by schedule and outcome
panels.description: Batch runs per schedule: ok, error, or empty (nothing due). Only empty batches for a long time while providers are connected means the due queries or the shard schedule stopped.

panels.title: batch errors / min by step
panels.description: Batch-level failures by step: blackhole_due / full_due (operator API), pins (geolocation certificate pins), blackhole_run / full_run (the batch itself), blackhole_submit (ingest), canceled (task drain). Any sustained step here is prober-side.

panels.title: providers handled / min (full schedule)
panels.description: Full-schedule batch tallies: attempted, submitted, skipped (no budget left), failed.

panels.title: providers handled / min (blackhole schedule)
panels.description: Blackhole-schedule batch tallies: checked, dark (checks that failed, tunnel failures included -- not the dark verdict, which takes three failed checks in a row), tunnel_failed. Checks that measured nothing are counted on *not measured providers*.

panels.title: batch duration p95 by schedule
panels.description: Wall clock of one batch. Climbing toward the task's max time means batches are being cut short by the deadline.

panels.title: scored ok/total ratio per probed provider
panels.description: Distribution of each probed provider's scored ratio (ok loads / scored loads after retries; canaries, sites on probation and loads not measured are left out). Healthy fleets pile up at 1.0. The mass sliding down uniformly across every bucket at once is a prober or platform fault; a growing 0 bucket with the rest unchanged is providers going dead.

panels.title: health ratio p10 / p50 (all probed providers)
panels.description: Tail and median of the per-provider scored ratio over time. p10 falling while p50 holds means a minority of providers degrading; both falling together is systematic.

panels.title: due selection and reporter completion boundaries
selection and submission capabilities by process
panels.description: Executable capabilities per process: 1 reports API selected-return observations, API earliest absolute deadline scheduling before unlocated work, or taskworker post-call submission observations. These are not proof of successful probes or fleet-wide rollout; absent series remain no-data. Country, class, and destination filters do not apply to these identity-free boundary metrics.

panels.title: due selection requests / s
panels.description: Per-API-process requests whose model selection returned, including empty selections. This counts the completed selection boundary, not response delivery or probe execution. Reset-aware rates preserve no-data when the exporter or required samples are absent.

panels.title: due selected-return events / s by lane
panels.description: Actual selected-return events by owning earliest-deadline lane (no-location, stale-location, stale-health, missing-health) and expiry at selection. Repeated selections are not unique providers, executed probes, receipt acknowledgments, or durable writes. Rate each process counter before summing; missing telemetry remains no-data.

panels.title: probe reporter completion outcomes / s
panels.description: Counts completed reporter calls for health and attempt submissions: acknowledged, unsupported, canceled, or error_or_unknown. An acknowledged call is not durable history and these are not probe success/failure measurements. Rate each process counter before summing; missing telemetry remains no-data. Durable provider state remains the fleet snapshot/direct-database boundary.

panels.title: egress site pool: prober and refresh events
batch guard trips
panels.description: Batches the prober held to be its own fault (geomap §11.3). A blackhole trip is a batch whose dark share was over 20 %: its negatives were discarded and are re-checked after the backoff. A full trip is a batch whose scored-load failure share was over 30 %: it was not submitted and is re-queued, so no provider's index moved. Each is counted once, by the taskworker where it happened, so this is the fleet's total over the trailing five minutes: any non-zero value is a trip, and any trip is the prober-fault finding of monitor signal §2.19b. The share each guard judged is on the providers dashboard.

panels.title: not measured providers
panels.description: Providers per schedule whose run or check measured nothing because its tunnel died and could not be re-created: the prober's lost path, never a verdict on the provider (geomap §11.3). Each is counted once, by the taskworker where it happened, so this is the fleet's total over the trailing five minutes; a sustained rise is the prober losing tunnels, not providers failing.

panels.title: destination pool fetches
panels.description: Destination pool fetches at the start of each pass, by result: server when the prober loaded the pool the server serves, builtin when that fetch failed and the prober fell back to its built-in table. Each is counted once, by the taskworker where it happened, so this is the fleet's total over the trailing five minutes; any builtin value is passes that probed the built-in sites instead of the refreshed pool.

panels.title: site pool refresh runs
panels.description: Pool refresh runs by result: refreshed, skipped (the fleet-wide failure share of the loads that reached their provider was over the 20 % prober-fault line, or fewer than the 20 % prober-fault floor of the recent loads reached their provider at all), or failed. Each is counted once, by the taskworker where it happened, so this is the fleet's total over the trailing five minutes: any non-zero value is a run; a skip is the refresh keeping a prober fault from emptying the pool, and failures with no refresh after them are the refresh-not-running finding of monitor signal §2.19b.

panels.title: site pool changes
panels.description: The changes each refresh made to the pool: sites retired, candidates promoted onto probation, sites graduated from probation, and places marked incompatible for a site or unmarked after their canaries passed. Each is counted once, by the taskworker where it happened, so this is the fleet's total over the trailing five minutes: any non-zero value is a change; the refresh is daily, so changes arrive once a day, at most one retirement per class.

panels.title: URL quota four hours after first admission
Known mature providers at URL quota
panels.description: Ten unique accepted measured successes or failures in the trailing four hours, among providers with a first-admission timestamp at least four hours old. Known newcomers and unknown first-admission age are separate. A known mature reading of 100% does not prove whole-fleet coverage while unknown age is nonzero, nor sustained coverage. N/A means zero mature denominator or unavailable evidence. TLS security and the 4/5 success quality ratio remain separate. One atomic global snapshot from exactly one current shard-zero owner; source and scrape clocks must be within 180 seconds, at most 30 seconds future, and newer than its process start. Global publisher replicas are never summed. Missing, tied, stale, mixed or incomplete evidence shows no data; monitor signal §2.19f additionally validates desired inventory and shard geometry.

targets.expr: max(((urnetwork_url_probe_admission_cohort{env="$env",job="taskworker",instance!="",state="quota_complete",cohort="mature"} / ignoring(state) urnetwork_url_probe_admission_cohort{env="$env",job="taskworker",instance!="",state="eligible",cohort="mature"}) and ignoring(state) (urnetwork_url_probe_admission_cohort{env="$env",job="taskworker",instance!="",state="eligible",cohort="mature"} > 0)) and on(env,job,host,block,instance) ((((((urnetwork_url_probe_fleet_observed_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",job="taskworker",instance!=""}) >= time() - 180) and ((urnetwork_url_probe_fleet_observed_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",job="taskworker",instance!=""}) <= time() + 30)) and (((timestamp(urnetwork_url_probe_fleet_observed_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",job="taskworker",instance!=""})) >= time() - 180) and panels.description: Currently eligible providers first admitted less than four hours ago, including those already at quota. One atomic global snapshot from exactly one current shard-zero owner; source and scrape clocks must be within 180 seconds, at most 30 seconds future, and newer than its process start. Global publisher replicas are never summed. Missing, tied, stale, mixed or incomplete evidence shows no data; monitor signal §2.19f additionally validates desired inventory and shard geometry.

panels.title: URL and probe diagnostic capabilities by process
panels.description: Executable capabilities and contract versions per taskworker. 1 means the process exports that bounded identity-free observation. An absent capability is no-data, not disabled or healthy.

panels.title: completed URL turn stage and tunnel setup timing
completed URL batch stage wall time / s
panels.description: Wall-clock stages of the same returned one-provider URL batches. check_and_buffer includes asynchronous route setup; total excludes still-running batches.

panels.title: completed URL timing coverage / min
panels.description: Returned batches with complete stage timing, batches with a closed setup observation, closed owned tunnels by strict admission timing coverage, and matched tunnels with an observed or missing source InEvaluation event. None is a success or durable coverage counter.

panels.title: tunnel setup calls / min
panels.description: Returned credential acquisition or processed-registration constructor calls in the completed turn cohort by stage and outcome (calls can overlap and include cleanup), wrapper calls still pending when an owned tunnel froze, and tunnels whose terminal Close returned an error.

panels.title: tunnel setup mean residence
panels.description: Mean returned setup call residence by stage and outcome (not a wall-time partition), and the mean source InEvaluation-to-Added time for matched tunnels with both events, which includes contract transport and send admission but not ping RTT.

panels.title: tunnel setup route stage seconds / s
panels.description: Source-time stages from credential entry to the first observed Added for matched unique constructors. All four stages share the matched tunnel denominator.

panels.title: initial ping, DNS waves, probe auth and probe credentials
initial-ping evaluations / min
panels.description: Evaluations started after successful construction, and terminal evaluations by outcome and dependency snapshot. acknowledged is not admission, and terminal cells are independent of accepted URL outcomes.

panels.title: initial-ping mean terminal residence
panels.description: Mean whole terminal residence per evaluation, including contract and carrier work, by outcome and dependency snapshot and by the exact ping path witnesses. These are terminal snapshots, not phase durations.

panels.title: initial-ping path evaluations / min
panels.description: Terminal evaluations by the exact local route-write and ACK callback witnesses. accepted is not remote receipt, and callback success is not a measured outcome.

panels.title: private-tunnel DNS waves / min
panels.description: Completed waves by local outcome and same-tunnel setup state, by the exact tunnel's end-of-wave contract witness (not_proved is an unknown cause), and by endpoint route snapshot. None is a provider verdict.

panels.title: DNS wave wall seconds / s
panels.description: DNS wave residence by contract witness (not contract-acquisition time), and seconds before or after the observed route admission. Before admission is not continuous setup time.

panels.title: probe auth, credentials and resident retirement / min
panels.description: Logical synchronous probe auth calls by last POST phase and outcome; internal prober credential operations; and owned probe resident capture and conditional removal. None measures provider coverage.

panels.title: blackhole and full batch progress, and the auxiliary egress tally
blackhole and full batch states in flight
panels.description: Currently owned batch and provider states. Blackhole completed_buffered includes unmeasured and guardable results; full queued includes selected work not started and finished_waiting includes failed or unmeasured work before its batch returns.

panels.title: blackhole and full worker events / min
panels.description: Actual worker lifecycle events. Blackhole completed means retained before guard and publication; full provider_finished is the ProbeOne return including teardown, not a successful or durable measurement.

panels.title: blackhole submissions and publication rows / min
panels.description: Nonempty batch calls by returned outcome (acknowledged is not a measured-row count), and payload rows at submit entry and by returned outcome. Acknowledged can be a replay or no-op; no result proves current eligibility.

panels.title: blackhole results and negative dispositions
panels.description: Completed check callbacks per minute by original result before the cohort guard, ordinary negatives per minute by cohort disposition (guard_eligible is not a durable dark verdict), and negatives awaiting their cohort decision now.

panels.title: blackhole pipeline decisions and due reads / min
panels.description: Pipeline entry, lookup, selection and first admission-stop decisions (not task identities or durable verdicts), and returned cheap due-read attempts by error class including retries.

panels.title: blackhole site-load retry waits
panels.description: Site load attempts sleeping between blackhole retries now (several can belong to one worker), and retry waits started and ended per minute, including cancellation.

panels.title: full successor selection / min
panels.description: Bounded full successor lookahead outcomes. prefix_exhausted means no unseen row in that bounded response, not an empty fleet backlog.

panels.title: auxiliary egress tally handoffs and rollups / min
panels.description: Auxiliary tally handoffs by accepted, unavailable, invalid or full outcome on every service that hands one off (never measured quota credits), tally rollup drains by outcome and by why reading ended, and the records they read. A calls, rows, time or error stop leaves retained records for the shard's next claim. SQL commitment is recorded by the durable task receipt.

panels.title: auxiliary egress tally backlog by shard
panels.description: Retained tally records or bytes as a fraction of each place shard's admission bound, whichever is fuller. Handoffs are refused as full at 100%. A drain that keeps up holds about two claims of a shard's runs. Read at the first call of each owner's latest drain, after at most one page of cleanup, so within 256 records of the occupancy producers met at the claim. Each taskworker publishes a shard's depth for five minutes after it reads it; the maximum across taskworkers is the fleet view.

panels.title: auxiliary egress tally oldest pending record by shard
panels.description: Age of each place shard's oldest unacknowledged tally record at the first call of its owner's latest drain: about one claim interval when the owner keeps up, rising while a backlog grows. Each taskworker publishes it for five minutes after it reads the shard; the maximum across taskworkers is the fleet view.

panels.title: auxiliary egress tally retained records and bytes by shard
panels.description: Tally records (left) and record bytes (right) each place shard retained, including committed records its next claim deletes. Handoffs are refused as full at 16384 records or 16 MiB. Read at the first call of each owner's latest drain, after at most one page of cleanup, so within 256 records of the occupancy producers met at the claim. Each taskworker publishes a shard's depth for five minutes after it reads it; the maximum across taskworkers is the fleet view.

panels.title: auxiliary egress tally owner read age by shard
panels.description: Seconds since any taskworker last completed the first call of a drain of each place shard (left): about one claim interval while its owner runs, rising without bound when the owner is stuck, for example failing its first call. The observed time is never withheld. Right: shards that no taskworker draining tally shards has read since it started.

panels.title: URL probe passes held and pass limit by taskworker
panels.description: The URL shard passes each taskworker instance may hold at once, read from the probe geometry when it starts (instance_url_concurrency over the per-pass URL concurrency, at most the shard count), beside the passes it holds now. A fleet whose limits add up to fewer passes than the configured shards leaves shards waiting for a free instance.

panels.title: in-process operator calls (taskworkers with operator_transport: local)
in-process operator calls / min by method
panels.description: Operator calls that taskworkers with operator_transport: local ran in-process, by operator method: the counterpart of the API dashboard's per-route request rate for the operator routes, which these calls never reach. A taskworker that keeps the operator API, the default, publishes none of these series; its calls are on the API dashboard.

panels.title: in-process operator call mean duration by method
panels.description: Mean time an in-process operator call ran in its call slot, by operator method, on taskworkers with operator_transport: local: the counterpart of the API's per-route handler duration. Each call's 30-second bound covers its wait for a slot and this time together.

panels.title: in-process operator calls running and waiting by taskworker
panels.description: In-process operator calls running in their passes' call slots, and calls waiting for one, on each taskworker with operator_transport: local. Running stays at or below operator_concurrency times the URL passes the taskworker holds (8 x 2 at Main's geometry), which keeps probe ingest from taking the taskworker's database pool; a steady waiting count means the bound, not the database, is pacing ingest.

panels.title: in-process operator call errors / min by method and kind
panels.description: In-process operator calls on taskworkers with operator_transport: local that did not end in an answer the API gives as success. refused: the API would have answered 4xx; failed: a 5xx answer, such as a panic or a done error while the caller still waited, or a local failure; canceled: the caller or the 30-second call bound ended a running call; unadmitted: the call ended waiting for a call slot and never ran.

panels.title: in-process operator mean call slot wait by method
panels.description: Mean wait for a call slot per in-process operator call, by operator method, on taskworkers with operator_transport: local: zero when a slot was free, and including calls that gave up waiting. It rises when operator_concurrency, not the database, is the bottleneck.
